summary: Discovery/PoC scoping focused on which hosting mode to use (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) for Windward's claim summarization model. Customer has strict EEA data residency, wants 6-week pilot, success criteria around latency (p50/p95), throughput, and cost per 1k tokens. Discussed tradeoffs: hosted for speed of start, dedicated for predictable throughput and lower unit cost, private/on-prem for regulated models. Agreed to run benchmark with sample prompts and report back with tuned config and SOW.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-12-28 15:00 UTC — Duration 62m — Attendees: Mark, Priya, Diego (Redwood); Tom, Lena, Rajiv, Maya, Oliver (Windward)

Summary (auto): PoC scoping for claim summarization and redaction workflows. Focus on deployment mode choice, success metrics, bench plan.

Topics: success criteria, workload sizing, benchmarks, timelines, security & residency, cutover constraints

[00:00:00] Mark (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining on a late December call, we'll go, um, about an hour and scope the pilot. quick intros?
[00:00:18] Tom - Windward CTO: Tom here, i'll start — we're trying to replace a heavyweight rules+nlp pipeline with a lighter LLM-driven summarizer for first-pass claims triage. main concerns are latency, cost, and regulatory (EEA residency).
[00:00:32] Priya (Redwood SE): thanks Tom. to confirm — workload today is roughly 500k tokens/day with spiky patterns during batch windows, is that still accurate?
[00:00:40] Lena - Head of ML: yes that's right, peak bursts in morning and evening, about 120 reqs/s target during peak; average request is ~450 tokens per response, some are 1k tokens for longer summaries.
[00:00:54] Diego (Redwood SA): ok so that informs batching and instance sizing — do you need anonymization before sending payloads off to hosted infra?
[00:01:05] Maya (Security): sensitive PII has to be redacted for hosted unless we have contractual guarantees. main ask: SOC2, data residency to EEA region, KMS for keys.

[00:01:22] Mark: perfect, so three hosting options: hosted-api (fastest to start), dedicated reserved pools (predictable throughput), private (VPC or on-prem) for fully isolated. walk us through what you care about most and a target timeline for pilot?
[00:01:36] Oliver (Product): timeline: 6 weeks to pilot, ideally live canary into 2 internal claim queues. success criteria: p50 < 80ms, p95 < 300ms end-to-end for 512-token responses, throughput 120 req/s sustained for 10m with graceful degradation. cost target TBD but we want to understand unit economics.
[00:02:00] Priya: note — those latency targets are 3-tier: hosted can usually hit low-latency with our shared infra; dedicated gives stronger tail-latency guarantees; private depends on your on-prem network and hardware. quantization choices and model family matter too (we should test 7B vs 13B).
[00:02:20] Rajiv (SRE): if we go private, SRE will need a clear cutover plan, maintenance windows, and remote support constraints — we can't have 20% p95 regressions during business-critical hours.

[00:02:36] Mark: ok let's map success criteria into measurable checkpoints: 1) correctness/quality (ROUGE or manual eval — threshold 0.78), 2) latency/throughput (Oliver's numbers), 3) cost-per-1k tokens below our pilot threshold, and 4) security reqs met (SOC2, KMS, audit logs). does that align?
[00:02:55] Lena: yes but add model stability — no more than 3% regression in NER/redaction metrics vs baseline during pilot.

[00:03:08] Diego: for benchmarking plan I propose three phases: microbench (single-model latency/profiles), scaled bench (simulate 120 req/s with realistic token mix), and long-run cost test (24hr run to measure KV cache effectiveness and cold-starts).
[00:03:23] Mark: excellent. quick Q from our side — do you have constraints on outbound peering for hosted? i.e., can we route to eu-west region or do you require on-prem?
[00:03:33] Maya: prefer eu-central for residency, but we need contract language stating logs and payloads do not leave region. on-prem would be ideal for models using internal actuarial tables.

[00:03:45] Priya: that maps well. tradeoffs to surface for decision maker: time-to-pilot, unit cost, SLO certainty, and operational overhead. Hosted: fastest, less ops, but need contractual residency; Dedicated: reserved GPUs in EU region, predictable throughput and lower token cost, can attach to enterprise VPC; Private: full isolation, highest ops overhead & longer lead time.

[00:04:12] Tom: what's the expected lead time for private?
[00:04:15] Diego: depends — if on-prem and air-gapped, 8-12 weeks for packaging & installs plus validation. VPC-hosted private (customer-managed VPC peering) is typically 3-4 weeks if firewall rules and peering are straightforward.

[00:04:31] Rajiv: that's a hard ask if we want 6-week pilot. we probably can't do full on-prem in 6 weeks.
[00:04:36] Mark: so realistic options to hit 6 weeks are: Hosted with EEA residency commitment, or Dedicated reserved pool in EU with quick network setup; Private on-prem is a longer path.

[00:04:50] Oliver: cost sensitivity — if dedicated reduces unit cost by 20% we may prefer it, but does Redwood allow a burst model for spiky traffic?
[00:04:59] Priya: yes, Dedicated has configurable burst capacity and autoscaling policies. we can configure a baseline reserved plus burst headroom. autoscale reacts to queue depth and token consumption.

[00:05:12] Lena: on evaluation metrics: we want deterministic comparisons — test same prompts across model family, measure p50/p95, token count, and then run human eval on 100 samples for quality. is that doable?
[00:05:22] Priya: absolutely. we'll include an eval harness, and can attach our prompt suite runner to your test data (PII redacted or synthetic).

[00:05:34] Maya: security Qs — do you provide customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM)? what about audit logs retention and SSO?
[00:05:42] Mark: yes, for Dedicated and Private you can integrate with your KMS; Hosted supports customer-managed keys in EU regions for enterprise plans. audit logs retention is configurable — we'll send the security packet. SSO via SAML/Okta supported.

[00:06:00] Tom: can Redwood run inference on quantized 4-bit models to reduce cost?
[00:06:05] Priya: yes, runtime supports multiple quantization profiles; we'll recommend quantization based on your quality bar. note: aggressive quantization may slightly affect rouge/NER. we'll include that in bench plan.

[00:06:18] Diego: operational cutover notes — if you choose dedicated, we recommend a canary targetting 10% of traffic for 2 weeks, with automatic fallback to hosted on regression. we can instrument rollout with tracing and per-route cost counters.

[00:06:35] Rajiv: fallback is important — we want clear rollback triggers.
[00:06:38] Mark: agreed. we'll propose rollback policies in SOW.

[00:06:45] Oliver: a question on metrics: how do you measure tokenized counts and billing surpises? can we get per-route and token-type breakdowns?
[00:06:54] Diego: yes, Redwood Console provides token-level breakdown, per-route cost, and per-model cost. we'll show a sample dashboard in the demo phase.

[00:07:05] Lena: for bench inputs, we'll send 3 classes of prompts: short detection, medium summary, long summary (1k tokens). also provide expected redact flags.

[00:07:16] Mark: great — for the pilot, propose success gates across weeks: week 0-1: connect and run microbench, week 2: scaled bench (120 req/s spike tests), week 3-4: human eval and long-run cost test, week 5-6: canary internal queue + final SOW decision.

[00:07:33] Tom: that fits the 6-week ask if we pick hosted/dedicated.

[00:07:40] Maya: if we go hosted, contract needs to state that logs/payloads are stored only in EU and keys are in our KMS. otherwise we need private.

[00:07:51] Mark: we'll mark that as an absolute requirement for hosted to be considered.

[00:07:57] Priya: operational detail for bench — we'll simulate KV-cache hit rates (0%, 30%, 70%) to see cost delta. prefix caching for claim ids can reduce token counts significantly.
[00:08:09] Lena: can Redwood's runtime do prefix caching across requests? we have many similar policy preambles.
[00:08:15] Diego: yes, automatic prefix/KV caching is part of the runtime; bench will measure real cost savings.

[00:08:25] Oliver: competitor question — we evaluated Mistral Cloud and Anthropic, they hit similar latencies but had differing pricing models. what differentiates Redwood here operationally?
[00:08:36] Mark: two things — production-first tooling (per-route dashboards, tracing, rollouts) and flexible hosting choices with predictable reserved capacity and on-prem options. plus focused guidance on cost-performance tradeoffs.

[00:08:50] Maya: do you do SOC2 + ISO attestation?
[00:08:53] Mark: SOC2 Type II yes, ISO in progress — full details in the packet.

[00:09:00] Priya: ok demo/bench logistics: we'll need a 3-hour lab window where we run scaled bench; prefer to run during your low-traffic window but still with real token distribution. Rajiv, which day is best for firewall changes?
[00:09:12] Rajiv: week of Jan 9 we have a maintenance slot on Tuesday/Thursday afternoons UTC.

[00:09:20] Mark: we'll propose Jan 10 or 12 for bench kickoff.

[00:09:26] Tom: can you send a sample benchmark plan and the minimal telemetry we need to expose?
[00:09:31] Priya: yes, we'll send the bench plan and a runbook that lists required metrics (p50/p95, CPU/GPU utilization, token counts, cache hit rate, model traces).

[00:09:44] Oliver: what about rollback and fallthrough — if model quality dips in canary, we need to revert fast. you mentioned automatic fallback to hosted — how fast is that?
[00:09:53] Diego: routing policies can be sub-1min to switch, with health checks; we'll instrument automatic fallback but prefer manual gating for first canary.

[00:10:05] Lena: about quality tests — would you run BLEU/ROUGE and some entity-level recall tests? we need SLOs on redaction accuracy.
[00:10:13] Priya: yes, we'll include entity-level metrics and custom checks for redaction to ensure PII isn't leaked.

[00:10:22] Mark: okay let's capture open risks: 1) residency contract language for hosted; 2) on-prem lead time if chosen; 3) cost uncertainty if quantization affects quality.
[00:10:34] Maya: added risk: audit log retention and access controls need to meet Windward internal policy.

[00:10:40] Mark: agreed — we'll include all in SOW.

[00:10:45] Tom: are there any network / egress costs to expect from Redwood if we do dedicated in EU?
[00:10:52] Mark: standard egress rules apply; we'll surface expected network egress costs in pilot pricing. typically minimal compared to token compute but we'll quantify.

[00:11:03] Priya: in bench we'll test 7B vs 13B to compare latency and quality; recommend we start with 13B quantized if quality is critical, fallback to 7B for lower unit cost if acceptable.

[00:11:18] Oliver: ok — let's talk deliverables: Redwood to share security packet, bench plan, SOW draft, pricing, and schedule. Windward to supply sample dataset and firewall peering details.

[00:11:30] Mark: exactly. anything else from Windward side?
[00:11:33] Rajiv: just that we need a contact to coordinate the peering and open specific ports — i'll be the SRE lead.
[00:11:39] Mark: noted. Priya and Diego will coordinate.

[00:11:44] Maya: one more security Q — can logging omit raw payloads in hosted logs? we want redacted logs forwarded to our SIEM.
[00:11:51] Diego: yes, we support log filters and can redact payloads at ingestion or only forward metadata. we'll detail options in the packet.

[00:12:05] Tom: good, that's a helpful answer.

[00:12:10] Mark: wrap up — recap next steps: Redwood to send security packet by Jan 4, bench kickoff week of Jan 9 (Mark to propose exact date), Redwood to provide SOW & pricing by Jan 7, Windward to provide sample prompts and SRE contact info by Jan 6.
[00:12:28] Oliver: agreed.
[00:12:30] Lena: thanks everyone.
[00:12:33] Mark: thanks, we'll follow up via email and schedule the bench. Happy holidays.

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mis-heard acronyms (e.g., KMS transcribed as "K and S"), filler words, slight speaker attribution drift on two short interjections.
